**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Two layers, both refuse by named diagnostic and neither can pass silently: generation (`crates/app/src/operation/rotary_gate.rs:108-119`, only when `unwind_c` actually grew the path and `c_rated` is false) and the lathe post backstop (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `liveMove`, rapid + C travel stated + no C rate + `|dc|>1e-9`), which also covers C-turning link rapids that are not orbits.
- Does not over-refuse: a machine stating a C feed or rapid is untouched (the gate's `c_rated` matches the post's `speeds.normal`/`rapid` reading); a machine with no C travel never reaches the unwind branch and `liveCTravel` stays false; a path that fits the travel is not refused (`wide` case in the e2e test); the opening-stretch shift adds no move and is not refused. The section-opening G00 C branch precedes the new check.
- No unwrap/expect/panic in product code; `c_rated` guards finite and positive. Decision file `docs/decisions/906-c-unwind-rate-cap.md` records the choice and the dropped default-rate option. No goldens, snapshots, process files or dependencies touched; no new modules. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #906`.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main f490458; already up to date, no conflicts)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| app lib | 111 passed |
| c_axis_fixture / c_axis_live / c_axis_unwind | 2 / 4 / 7 passed |
| lathe_post / lathe_post_refusals | 7 / 6 passed |
| posting / golden_cl | 17 / 25 passed (goldens unchanged) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Overlap with #951 (shared rotary feed cap, #885): both edit `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove`, but in different hunks. A `git merge-tree` of the two heads is clean. Semantically they compose: #964's refusal sits before the F cap, so an unrated C-travel machine is still refused after #951, which keeps `liveCRate` as the C rate input. Either order works; whichever merges second should re-run `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_refusals` and `c_axis_*` (#951's cap changes F for rated machines, so the second PR may need to re-check the `rated.warnings.is_empty()` assertion here).
2. The gate quick plan did not list `lathe_post*`/`posting`/`golden_cl` even though the .cps changed; I ran them anyway and they pass.
3. A machine with neither C travel nor C rate still posts uncapped C rapids (pre-existing, noted in the decision file); `fanuc.cps`/`doosan-dnm.cps` still have no cap (#951 addresses those).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d1e1245a531e39f4b228ae6715429385115f0efc -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Independent review (not the author's), high tier - this PR changes posted G-code.

### What looks good
- The named-refusal option is taken and recorded with its reasons and the dropped alternative (`docs/decisions/906-c-unwind-rate-cap.md`).
- Two layers, both fed from the machine file's rotary C entry (`AxisLimits.feed`/`rapid`/`travel`, mirrored to `rotaries[].speeds.normal`/`rapid`/`travel` by `post::machine::mirror`): generation refuses an inserted rewind orbit (`rotary_gate.rs:114`), and the lathe post refuses any C-turning rapid on a C-travel/no-C-rate machine (`fanuc-lathe.cps:501`). The post refusal goes through `refuse()`, and `posting.rs:465` blocks the file on any post warning, so nothing is written - no uncapped F, no rewind silently dropped.
- Machines with a C rate: unchanged. The `two_rings` golden and every NC/CL golden are untouched, and the rated bench still posts with no warnings.
- Machines with no C travel: unchanged and not refused (the new branch is gated on `liveCTravel`).
- The message is plain English and names what the file lacks and the fix ("state the C axis's feed or rapid rate").
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests (the one `panic!` is in the unit test at `rotary_gate.rs:255`). `rotary_gate.rs` is 295 lines. The tests sit with the C-axis post suites.

### Local results (trial-merged with main a6bd69d8, clean merge)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all targets) | ok - lib 16, axis_direction_cli 3, comp 9, comp_plane 3, mch_head_search 2, post_engine 33 |
| app lib | 115 passed (incl. `rotary_gate::tests::a_rewind_without_a_stated_c_rate_is_refused_by_name`) |
| app `c_axis_unwind` | 7/7 |
| app `c_axis_live` | 4/4 |
| app `c_axis_fixture` | 2/2 |
| app `lathe_post` / `lathe_post_refusals` | 7/7, 6/6 |
| app `rotary_letter` / `machine` / `posting` | 3/3, 33/33, 17/17 |
| app `conformance` / `golden_cl` | 6/6, 25/25 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. **Generation and post draw the line in different places.** I ran a local probe (not pushed): on `unrated((-100000, 100000))`, Rotary Contour on the `c_axis_unwind` bar **generates** clean (your own test asserts "no rewind, no refusal"), but the lathe post then **refuses** it, because its ordinary link rapids turn C (`a C-axis rapid that turns C, but the machine file states a C travel but no C rate ...`). Refusing is the safe choice - those rapids would post at the same unbounded F. But the user sees a clean generate and then a post block, and the test comment at `c_axis_unwind.rs:323` ("the unstated rate matters only where a rewind would post") is not quite true for posting. Consider either moving the generation check to "any C-turning rapid" or rewording the comment and the decision file. For comparison, a stamped `two_rings` with no link rapid posts clean on the same machine.
2. **"Has a C rate" is worked out twice**, once in Rust (`c_rated`, `rotary_gate.rs:146`) and once in the script (the existing `liveCRate`, `fanuc-lathe.cps:443`). Both read the same machine-file fields, and `Machine` validation (`def.rs:260`) rules out NaN, infinite and non-positive rates, so they agree. If they ever disagreed, the only effect would be one extra refusal, never an unsafe post. Not blocking, but a later shared helper (or a machine-mirror flag) would keep them in step.
3. The decision file says generation refuses when the unwind "inserted an orbit or shifted a stretch's C". The code only refuses when moves are inserted (`unwound.moves.len() != stamped.moves.len()`), which matches the PR body's "a shift adds no move". The decision file should say the same.
4. Measured during the probe: on a machine with **no** C travel and no C rate, the same generated path still posts with no warning at **F152613.2**. That case predates this PR and is out of scope (you already noted it). #975 closes it.
5. **Overlap with #975 / #1025:** both branches already carry this PR's two commits (b21879ac, d1e1245a) and add to them, so there is no text conflict. #975 widens the same `liveMove` check to every no-rate machine (it drops the `liveCTravel` condition and keeps the travel wording in the message), which agrees with this PR's intent. #1025 carries #975 plus the face-drill exit. Advised merge order: #964, then #975, then #1025, each taking `git merge origin/main` after its parent lands.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
